disposition_reason: ICP-MS whole-blood germanium geometric means and percentiles for 1,302 residents of Shandong, China, overall and by sex, cosmetics, hair dye, age, alcohol, smoking and fried food strata.

study.method: ICP-MS (Thermo Fisher) on whole blood diluted 1:10 with 0.01% Triton X-100 and 0.5% nitric acid; yttrium internal standard
lod: Blood Ge LOD 0.18 µg/L after tenfold dilution factor (pp. 3 to 4)
study.qa: Tube and vial blank testing; single-point standard checks every 30 samples; spike recovery 90.0 to 112.4% across Zn, Ge, Pb; no CRM reported

findings.group: Total population; residents aged 6 to 60 years, Qingdao, Jinan and Heze, Shandong, China, 2009 to 2010
findings.notes: Blood concentration per liter; not converted to µg/kg. LOD 0.18 µg/L (p. 4). Percentiles as printed.
findings.statistic_raw: GM (95% CI) with P5 to P95

unresolved: Zinc and lead rows (Tables 1 and 3) are outside this element and were not recorded.
Text on p. 6 transposes the alcohol subgroup geometric means relative to Table 2; Table 2 values recorded.
non_numeric_findings: Authors state germanium intake is through water, food or drugs and that excessive germanium can damage kidneys, nervous system and lungs (p. 2, background citing other work).
Blood germanium increased with reported fried food frequency; the authors state the reasons require further study (p. 8).
